contracts.superseded_reason: owner delegation, 1 Nov 2026: the lead accepted four definitions the SO-F-09 text leaves open (a stub session is an agent subject or a raw status op; a verification record may be written by a person, operator or service; 'by' is set from the resolved credential, so a caller-supplied by is ignored and an agent in the personal scope resolves to an agent subject; withholding is strict, and an entity or owner with no source is hidden from a partial view) and SO-F-09.2 writes them in and pins them with criteria, marks who may adjudicate, verify and dismiss and the confirm and reject outcomes as provisional until ADR 5 and SO-A-05; it limits dismissal to person and operator subjects (ADR 5 safe default: ungated stays denied; an agent or a service cannot dismiss); the scope adds only src/engine/identity.mjs, because the signed scope already lists changelog.d/SO-F-09.md and docs/MODULES.md

contracts.supersedes_reason: owner delegation, 1 Nov 2026: the lead accepted four definitions the SO-F-09 text leaves open (a stub session is an agent subject or a raw status op; a verification record may be written by a person, operator or service; 'by' is set from the resolved credential, so a caller-supplied by is ignored and an agent in the personal scope resolves to an agent subject; withholding is strict, and an entity or owner with no source is hidden from a partial view) and SO-F-09.2 writes them in and pins them with criteria, marks who may adjudicate, verify and dismiss and the confirm and reject outcomes as provisional until ADR 5 and SO-A-05; it limits dismissal to person and operator subjects (ADR 5 safe default: ungated stays denied; an agent or a service cannot dismiss); the scope adds only src/engine/identity.mjs, because the signed scope already lists changelog.d/SO-F-09.md and docs/MODULES.md
contracts.superseded_reason: owner delegation, 1 Nov 2026: raw applyOp and the replay of the op log still take the 'by' of a record as written, so a forged by on a finding operation that went around Graph.bindFindingEvent counts as the subject it names; pull request #362 records this as open work. SO-F-09.3 writes in definition 5: the effective by is derived from the flat credential descriptor on the record itself (rec.credential, a top-level field), as of rec.ts with a validated ts; data.by is ignored for authority; the actor's scope is held against the finding's scope; evidence operations on a finding need a credential; OpLog.append accepts only a resolved actor and refuses, with code clock_behind, a credentialed record whose ts is below the floor of its device (the largest ts of that device's credentialed records, by Date.parse, computed lazily on its first credentialed append and cached) and, with code clock_floor_invalid, a credentialed append of a device whose credentialed chain holds a ts that does not parse. The descriptor is a trust carrier that is not authenticated, the log is only as trusted as its writer, and signing the log is a separate decision. It pins this with seventeen new criteria (37 in all, the 20 of SO-F-09.2 carried with their statements verbatim and their commands unpiped). The scope adds src/engine/oplog.mjs and test/oplog.test.mjs; the record base is b5932d3; the trust carrier may change when ADR 8 is decided, and role-binding scope is deferred to PG-W-21B
